Idempotent V3→V4 migration trigger, called when a research is opened in the V4 UI (ENG-18919).

Four outcomes, so a user returning to an old V3 task in the new UI is never stuck:
- Already-agentic (native V4 or previously migrated) → no-op; the normal V4 flow owns it.
- Finished legacy V3 (full analysis complete, ``is_v3_finished``) → migrate to agentic WITHOUT
  running the fill (mark_research_agentic): the task lands as a normal V4 task with every action
  unlocked, its already-complete content untouched (no run, no charge).
- Unfinished legacy V3 → migrate to agentic and auto-run the fill exactly once (the flag flip makes
  every later open take the already-agentic branch), charging as for a normal full-research run.
- V4 disabled in this env → render as-is (no migrate).

Safe to call on every open: each branch is cheap and the migration is single-shot.

commit.

post.description:
REWRITE: regenerate the selected variant, leaving every attorney-edited paragraph untouched.

Uniform per variant, and one LLM call either way — the flat ``CREDIT_COSTS`` charge is honest
because every Rewrite now costs the same thing. Short is re-condensed from committed Extensive
(so rewriting Short also picks up edits made to Extensive); Extensive is a rewrite of its own
committed prose.

Extensive deliberately does NOT re-import the matter's Timeline & Facts task. The import is
seeding only: by the time this button exists the agent has authored or extended those paragraphs
and the attorney may have corrected them, and re-importing would throw all of that away. That
also removes the old "no linked timeline" 409 — nothing about this path needs a timeline.
ADD: attorney writes a paragraph directly (no LLM), appended to the end of the document.

delete.description:
DELETE: hard-remove one paragraph from one variant.

Intentionally hard-deletes even a durable TIMELINE-imported paragraph — an explicit attorney
delete is destructive by design, matching ``delete_coa``. The durable-preserve rule protects
imports from regeneration and agent-prune (the PUT/demote paths), not from a deliberate delete.

get.description:
READ: the documents that may be attached to a paragraph as evidence.

Exactly the set POST ``/sof_exhibits`` accepts, from the same helper the fill agent's citing paths
use (``resources/citable_documents.py``) — an attach the server would reject must be unofferable,
or the picker offers the attorney a button that fails.

post.description:
ADD: put a document in this research's exhibit registry and return the letter it was given.

No credit dependency, matching the paragraph-mutation routes above: this is a metadata write, not
a generation.

Returning the exhibit is what keeps letters server-owned. They are allocated by
``db/exhibits.py::next_exhibit_label`` and never re-lettered, so a client that guessed its own
label would eventually point two documents at one letter in the attorney's own notes. Idempotent
by source rather than by call — ``register_exhibit`` reuses the letter a document+page already
holds — so the client needs no dedup of its own either.

The FE fires this whenever the cases step is committed; this endpoint owns

Dedup order:

post.description:
Notify the backend that an assistant turn has been saved for this conversation.

Called by the frontend after persisting the AI response message to the
database.  Fires (or signals) a debounced Temporal workflow that will
eventually save the conversation as a TASK_MEMORY doc in doc hub and
trigger downstream matter-memory regeneration.

``body.count`` is forwarded to the debounce workflow so the message-count
cap tracks only qualifying messages (user inputs + final AI text responses),
not thinking blocks.  Defaults to 1 in all cases (body omitted or body
provided without an explicit count).

This endpoint is intentionally best-effort:
- If the Temporal trigger fails, the response still returns 200 and a
  warning is logged.  The next turn will try again.
- If the conversation is not linked to a matter (or memory is disabled),
  the downstream activity will skip the save silently.
- The context engine's live-collector fallback produces correct output
  even if this trigger never fires — it will just be slower on read.

persists it to DocHub, and charges credits — then returns a ``job_id``
immediately. The draft runs as a heartbeated Temporal activity on the general
worker, so it survives a page refresh, tab close, network drop, and even a full
web-process restart mid-draft; the frontend polls
GET /generate_agent/status/{job_id} for progress and the rendered file.

Standard Temporal status pattern: Temporal is the source of truth for terminal
state (the status endpoint reads it via describe()/result()), and the drafting
stepper is reported to the standard ``RedisStatusManager`` keyed by workflow id.

Gated by config.CONTRACT_DRAFTING_USE_DOC_AGENT; the legacy per-section
/generate path is unchanged and used when the flag is off.

total_steps, phase} while running, the rendered file (docx_base64 + filename +
doc_id) on completion, or {status:"error", message}. Authorized to the user who
started the job.

Follows the platform's standard Temporal status pattern: Temporal is the source
of truth for terminal state (running/done/failed) via ``describe()``/result(),
and the drafting stepper is read from the standard ``RedisStatusManager``.

get.description:
Check each configured Temporal worker base URL's ``GET /ready``.

**Configuration:** set env ``TEMPORAL_WORKER_HEALTH_BASE_URLS`` to a comma-separated list of
HTTPS bases (no path), e.g. both law and order for each worker type:

``https://temporal-file-processor-law....io,https://temporal-file-processor-order....io,...``

**Pass rule (blue/green):** for each worker family (e.g. ``file-processor`` derived from the
hostname), **at least one** side must return JSON ``{ "ready": true }``. Standalone sides that
are intentionally standby will not be ready; the opposite color must be polling Temporal.

**Auth:** ``TEMPORAL_AGGREGATE_HEALTH_TOKEN`` must be set to a non-empty secret; send header
``Authorization: Bearer <token>`` on every request. If the env var is missing or blank, this
endpoint returns ``503`` with an empty JSON body.

**Status codes:** ``200`` if every family has at least one ready worker; ``503`` if workers are
unhealthy or if ``TEMPORAL_AGGREGATE_HEALTH_TOKEN`` is not configured (empty body in the
latter case).
If ``TEMPORAL_WORKER_HEALTH_BASE_URLS`` is unset, returns ``200`` with ``status: disabled``
(still requires a valid Bearer token).

What storage already holds for blobs the caller is about to send.

A desktop upload interrupted by a closed laptop has two ways of having done
work that must not be repeated: a file whose bytes all arrived but whose
manifest never did, and a large file staged in blocks partway through. Both
questions are reads against blob storage.

Answered here rather than by the client so the upload SAS stays write-only.
A token that can read is a token that can take a customer's documents if it
leaks, and an interrupted upload is not worth that. This endpoint uses the
API's own credentials and answers only about the caller's own container --
the path is a blob name within it, so there is nothing to scope wrong.

Every failure answers "we do not know", which sends the file. Sending
something already there costs a transfer; skipping something that is not
costs the document.

one edit. Same response shape and the same budget verdict as ``/estimate``.

delete.description:
Delete a folder and cascade its contents. Matter: un-associate the subtree's docs
from the matter (docs survive in DocHub). DocHub: tombstone files whose only home is
the subtree (they vanish from listings immediately) and purge them in the background
via BulkDeleteWorkflow — restart-safe and non-blocking even for folders with thousands
of files; files also filed elsewhere are untagged. Empty folders just drop the row.

``prune_empty_folders`` additionally clears the folders this delete left empty — the
deleted folder's ancestor chain, plus the matter folders its files vacated — never
unrelated empty folders elsewhere in the scope (ENG-21711). Matter scope prunes inline
(synchronous); DocHub scope prunes after the background purge drains (so it can't race
the async doc removal). The UI should confirm against the listing's `total_file_count`
first. Requires edit on the scope.

schema.description: Also delete the deleted folder's ancestors if this delete left them with no files.

Add or remove a focus-area tag on a single event (ENG-15314).

Membership is binary in the UI; under the hood a manually-added tag is stored with the
maximum score (10) so it always ranks/filters as top-relevance for that area. Adds are
restricted to the dataset's existing focus areas; removing simply drops that dimension.
Does not change the event's overall relevance or mark the SoF out of sync.

post.description:
Incrementally (re)score events against newly-added focus areas (ENG-15313).

Call after editing the dataset's focus areas (add/edit). Starts a background workflow that
tags any new focus area, then scores only the not-yet-scored tags across existing events,
merging into ``focus_area_scores``. Returns immediately with the ``workflow_id`` so the
caller can poll ``GET .../focus-areas/rescore/status`` to drive the transient "Scoring
focus areas" indicator. No full timeline re-extraction; overall relevance is untouched.

indicator up until the scores land. Returns ``running=False`` for any unknown / terminal /
unreachable workflow so the indicator always clears (fail-safe, never sticks).

need (``listing_needed`` False, with ``listing_reason``). ``include_hidden`` is accepted and ignored,
and ``hidden_count`` is always 0; both remain only so existing clients keep working.

get.description:
List the downloadable exports for a dataset, newest first.

Hybrid lookup:

1. **DocHub-tagged exports** — query ``DocMetadata`` rows whose
   ``additional_info`` contains ``{"dataset_id": <id>, "export_type": ...}``.
   Returned with a populated ``doc_hub_doc_id`` and a ``download_url``
   wired to the existing ``/discovery/download?doc_hub_doc_id=...``
   route. That route resolves the blob via ``DocMetadata.location``,
   which is the blob path *at upload time* — so dataset renames don't
   break the link.
2. **Legacy fallback** — if no DocMetadata rows match, list Azure blobs
   under ``{dataset_id}/.export/`` in the dataset's container. Each
   blob becomes an entry with ``doc_hub_doc_id=None`` and a
   ``download_url`` pointing at ``/discovery/download?filename=...``
   (the original keyed-by-filename path). Pre-DocHub datasets stay
   discoverable without backfill.

The FE doesn't have to branch on which variant it got — it hits the
pre-built ``download_url`` either way.

post.description:
Delete Doc Hub, blobs, eDiscovery, analytics, and related work data.

Does not delete ``model_usage_ledger`` (retained for cost of deleted users).

Postgres and eDiscovery commits run **before** blob-container and vector-table
deletes so a failed commit cannot leave DB rows pointing at storage that
already gone. The two commits are independent databases (no 2PC): if
``db.commit()`` succeeds and ``ediscovery_db.commit()`` fails, Postgres work
data is already gone and a retry is idempotent. The response is 200 only
after both commits and the external deletes succeed.

``since``: ISO lower bound (inclusive) through now — mutually exclusive with ``month``.

Rows from ``HIDDEN_BACKGROUND_MODULES`` / ``HIDDEN_BACKGROUND_STEPS`` are
omitted so the panel only moves when the tester actually does something.
They are still charged and still stored; this endpoint just does not show
them.

Zero-credit rows are omitted too. ``credits_from_cost_usd`` is ``cost/0.02``
with no rounding, so a row charging real money always has credits > 0 and
this filter drops nothing current. What it does drop is the tracking-only
history from Aug 6-20 2026, when this ticket recorded ``cost_usd`` while
``effective_credits`` stayed 0 by design: those rows read as
"0.000000 credits / $0.01673360", which a non-technical tester would
reasonably report as a billing fault. They cannot surface as the newest row
today, so this is belt-and-braces — but the cost of being wrong is a
reopened ticket, and the cost of the guard is one predicate.

Trade-off accepted: if some future path ever records 0 credits for real
work, the panel will hide it rather than show a confusing zero. Query the
ledger directly to audit that case.

Ordered by ``created_at`` rather than ``id``: there is no ``(user_id, id)``
index, so ordering by the primary key degrades into a backward PK scan that
discards every other user's rows until it finds a match (measured on beta:
6,124 rows discarded / 5,149 buffers to return ONE row, growing with how
long the caller has been idle — and this endpoint is polled every 15s).
``idx_mul_user_created (user_id, created_at)`` serves this ordering
directly. Both columns are written at insert time, so the row order is the
same.

delete.description:
Delete a matter. Requires ``can_delete`` permission on the matter.

The two flags are independent; any combination is valid.  Concretely:

* No flags + tasks linked → 409 (caller must unlink or pass ``force``).
* No flags + no tasks → 204, matter deleted.
* ``force=true`` → linked tasks are detached (``matter_id`` cleared) and
  the matter is deleted.  Files survive as unassigned (the ``matter_docs``
  FK cascades the join row only, not the doc).  Returns 204.
* ``delete_files=true`` (with or without ``force``) → every file attached
  to the matter is queued for hard delete (DB row + Azure blob + vector
  store), including files also attached to other matters.  The purge runs
  in the background ``BulkDeleteWorkflow``; the files disappear from every
  listing immediately.  Returns 200 with :class:`MatterDeleteResponse`.
  Without ``force``, linked tasks still produce 409 first; the file-delete
  path only runs after the task check passes.  ``GET {id}/delete-impact``
  previews how many files are shared with other matters.

**Per-file authorization on ``delete_files=true``:** matter ``can_delete``
is treated as authority over every document attached to the matter,
including files uploaded by other team members.  No per-doc owner check
runs on this path (unlike ``/document/delete-document`` and
``/document/delete-documents``, which are per-doc owner-only).  The
intent is matter-teardown: an admin who deletes the matter is entitled
to clean up everything attached to it.  Callers who want to preserve a
specific contributor's files should detach them from the matter
(via ``POST /document/remove-from-matter``) before calling this with
``delete_files=true``.

**Why the purge is async (ENG-23658):** done inline, a matter with thousands
of files outlived the 240 s gateway timeout.  The client saw "failed" while
the request kept destroying blobs and vectors with its DB transaction still
open, so every retry blocked on its locks.

**Partial-failure semantics on ``delete_files=true``:** the matter is
**always** deleted on this path.  Files that could not be queued are returned
in ``files_failed`` and survive in the Unassigned view for manual retry; the
usual one is an archive still being extracted (ENG-22114), which is refused
outright.  The matter cannot be un-deleted to retry in place.

Token endpoint (RFC 6749 §3.2): authorization_code exchange or refresh_token rotation.

Find someone to act as: by name, email, user id or Stripe customer id.

The same fields the web admin search (``Admin/searchUsers.ts``) looks at,
without its credit arithmetic -- that costs a backend call per result and
a switcher needs none of it. Every field matches on part of its value,
case-insensitively, including the ids: an admin working from a log line or
a support ticket often has only the start of one. The web matches ids
exactly; the switcher's hint says partial, and one rule for every field is
the only kind a hint can describe honestly.

POST rather than GET so the search terms, which are usually an email, stay
out of access logs. Restricted to ``strongsuit-god`` like the grant: the
results are customer contact details, and only that role can use them here.

People who cannot be chosen are returned marked rather than left out, so an
admin looking for a colleague learns why the row is disabled instead of
concluding the person does not exist.

Exchange an admin's own desktop token for one scoped to a customer.

The rules are the web mint's (``Admin/mintImpersonationToken.ts``): only
``strongsuit-god``, never yourself, and never internal staff -- except that
the beta client may target staff, so a god user can reproduce what a tester
who holds an internal role is seeing.

The desktop client comes from the caller's own token, never from the
request. The beta client is the one allowed to target staff, and taking it
from the body would let the prod app claim to be beta and lift the block.

No refresh token is issued. The app mints again from the admin's own
session when this one runs out, so the admin's sign-in remains the only
long-lived credential, and revoking it ends acting-as within one lifetime.

Every mint is recorded in ``Usage`` before the token exists. If that write
fails, nothing is issued: an impersonation with no audit row is exactly
what the row is there to prevent.
Revoke a refresh token (RFC 7009). Always 200 so callers cannot probe token validity.
Sign the caller out of every desktop install. Requires the user's normal session.

BalanceSheetItemCreateRequest.title: BalanceSheetItemCreateRequest
BalanceSheetItemCreateRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /balance-sheet/items`` — manual entry from the UI.

Server-set fields (``source='human_entered'``, ``is_locked=True``,
``is_active=True``, ``normalized_dedup_key=NULL``) are intentionally not
part of this schema so a client cannot spoof an AI-inferred row or pin
a dedup key that would collide with future auto-population.

Back-link fields (``rental_property_id``, ``real_property_id``, etc.) are
also omitted — those are only set by the AI activity. The UI can still
record a free-form association via ``description`` / ``metadata_ex``.

BalanceSheetItemDetailResponse.title: BalanceSheetItemDetailResponse
BalanceSheetItemDetailResponse.description:
Single item with pairing eager-loaded for the detail page.

- ``secured_by_item`` is set when this row is a liability secured by an
  asset (the mortgage row carries a reference to the house it's against).
- ``securing_liabilities`` is the inverse list for assets (the house row
  carries the mortgage + HELOC that encumber it).

BalanceSheetItemResponse.title: BalanceSheetItemResponse
BalanceSheetItemResponse.description:
A single balance-sheet item — the row shape returned by list + detail.

All money lives on ``current_amount``; the ``kind`` discriminator picks the
sign at the consumer (assets count positive, liabilities count negative
toward net worth). The dollar value itself is always stored as a positive
amount.

BalanceSheetItemSummary.title: BalanceSheetItemSummary
BalanceSheetItemSummary.description:
Minimal balance-sheet item shape used for nested ``secured_by_item`` /
``securing_liabilities`` references on the detail response.

Avoids unbounded recursion (a detail response embedding full detail of its
paired items would be redundant and confusing).

BalanceSheetItemUpdateRequest.title: BalanceSheetItemUpdateRequest
BalanceSheetItemUpdateRequest.description:
Body for ``PATCH /balance-sheet/items/{item_id}`` — partial update.

``kind`` and ``dataset_id`` are deliberately not present: a row's
asset-vs-liability nature is fixed at creation (changing it would silently
flip the sign on net-worth math). ``source``, ``is_locked``, and
``is_active`` are also not present — the server sets ``is_locked=True``
on every successful PATCH; the lock cannot be cleared via this endpoint,
and active state is managed by DELETE.

``category`` is allowed to change for misclassification fixes (e.g. an
AI-tagged ``investment`` that's actually a ``retirement`` 401(k)).

BalanceSheetListResponse.title: BalanceSheetListResponse
BalanceSheetListResponse.description: Paginated list of balance-sheet items in a dataset.

BalanceSheetSummaryResponse.title: BalanceSheetSummaryResponse
BalanceSheetSummaryResponse.description:
Roll-up totals for the dataset's balance sheet.

Liability totals are stored and returned as **positive balances owed**;
``net_worth`` is ``total_assets - total_liabilities``. The UI does not
compute these — it reads them straight from this endpoint so a filter
change can't desync the totals.

resolved by ``income.py``'s bottom-of-module ``model_rebuild()`` call —
income.py is the natural load-order tail (real_estate imports from income,

``role`` is what the source document called them; ``ownership_pct`` is the
fractional share when disclosed (NULL when the source is silent, e.g. CP 575
names a responsible party but not the %); ``verified_by`` is the append-only
set of authoritative ``source_document_type`` values that have attested
this linkage (mirrors ``BusinessResponse.verified_by`` semantics — empty
means self-reported only); ``source_document_types`` is every doc that has

BusinessValuationEstimate.title: BusinessValuationEstimate
BusinessValuationEstimate.description:
LLM valuation output stored on the inputs row.

Every field is required (nullable where the model may decline) — OpenAI
strict structured output demands all properties appear in ``required``,
and free-form dicts are rejected, hence the fixed-key weights model.

Amounts are ``float``, not ``Decimal``, and must stay that way. Pydantic
renders ``Decimal`` as an ``anyOf`` carrying a regex with a negative
lookahead, which is outside the schema subset strict structured output
accepts. The request is then rejected before the model runs, and the API
reports it as ``status=incomplete incomplete_reason=max_output_tokens``
with zero tokens used — which reads like a token-limit problem and is not
one. Nothing is lost: the JSON on the wire is IEEE-754 either way. Convert
to ``Decimal`` at the point of persistence instead.

BusinessValuationEstimateResponse.title: BusinessValuationEstimateResponse
BusinessValuationEstimateResponse.description:
200 envelope for the estimate endpoint.

The endpoint always returns 200; callers branch on ``status`` rather than
HTTP code (our API gateway doesn't surface 4xx bodies to the frontend).
``estimate`` is populated only when ``status == "ok"``. ``insufficient_documents``
is an expected, user-actionable condition (no financial statements yet),
not an error — ``missing_statement_types`` lists what's still needed.

BusinessValuationParty.title: BusinessValuationParty
BusinessValuationParty.description:
One taxpayer's ownership / salary / distributions on a business.

Auto-filled values come from K-1 Section J, W-2 wages, business_members,
sole-prop defaults, and 1099-DIVs depending on the entity type. The
``*_override`` fields are the lawyer-entered values from
``business_valuation_party_inputs`` — when set, they take precedence
over the auto-filled value on UI displays and downstream computations.

BusinessValuationResponse.title: BusinessValuationResponse
BusinessValuationResponse.description:
Merged GET response: auto-fill values + lawyer overrides + statement aggregates.

Year keys (``*_by_year``) use the ISO calendar year string (``"2024"``)
when the statement's ``period_end`` falls in the 12-29 → 01-03 window,
otherwise the ISO date string (``"2024-06-30"``) so non-calendar fiscal
years remain distinguishable.

BusinessValuationUpdateRequest.title: BusinessValuationUpdateRequest
BusinessValuationUpdateRequest.description:
PUT body — only override-bearing fields are writable.

Auto-fill values (statement aggregates, K-1 section J, W-2 wages) are
NOT editable through this endpoint; they reflect the underlying
extracted documents.

BusinessWithCountsResponse.title: BusinessWithCountsResponse
BusinessWithCountsResponse.description:
Listing row — business plus aggregate K-1 / parent-return / member / account counts.

``k1_count`` is the number of Schedule K-1s issued by this entity (only
meaningful for S-Corps / partnerships). ``has_parent_return`` flips true
when the 1120 / 1120-S / 1065 itself has been extracted into the same
dataset. ``member_count`` reflects how many distinct Taxpayers we've tied
to this business (sole_member / member / shareholder / responsible_party).

``banking_account_count`` / ``liability_account_count`` / ``investment_account_count``
are the number of rows in ``financial_accounts`` / ``liability_accounts`` /
``investment_accounts`` whose ``business_id`` points at this entity. Each
is independent — a business may have a checking account but no credit
cards, or vice versa. The UI uses these to drive the per-section business
picker (only show businesses that actually have accounts in the section
being viewed).

filename.description: The file's display name (the SAME name you will send to /add-document, e.g. '05_Affidavit.pdf'). Enables path-aware duplicate detection (ENG-17767): byte-identical content at a DIFFERENT path is a distinct record (a symlink alias), not a duplicate, so 'skip' is returned only for a true no-op (same bytes+name at the same current path).

'alias' = the bytes exist elsewhere; do NOT upload — call /create-alias to hardwire a symlink record instantly (no Azure transfer, no ingest).

ClioCustomFieldValue.title: ClioCustomFieldValue
ClioCustomFieldValue.description:
A single custom field value from a Clio matter.

Clio custom fields can return different JSON types depending on the
``field_type`` configured in Clio:

- ``text_line``, ``text_area``, ``date``, ``url``, ``email``, ``picklist``
  → ``string`` (handled natively)
- ``numeric``, ``currency`` → ``number`` (coerced to str by the validator below)
- ``checkbox`` → ``boolean``
- ``multi_picklist`` → ``array`` of strings
- ``contact``, ``matter`` → ``object`` with ``id`` + ``name``/``display_number``

The validator below coerces all non-string types to ``str`` so that a
single unexpected field type never crashes the entire matter parse.

tools.title: Tools
tools.description: Deep search enables both supported retrieval tools by default.

doc_ids.title: Doc Ids
doc_ids.description: Allowlist of DocHub doc IDs the doc-search tool is restricted to. ``None`` applies no allowlist (tool searches its full default scope). An empty list yields zero retrieval candidates.

include_memory.title: Include Memory
include_memory.description: When False, the iteration-0 preload is skipped entirely — no MATTER_MEMORY, TASK_MEMORY, conversation messages, matter markdown, or doc summaries. Synthesis grounds purely on retrieval results. Used by the task-only path to enforce no matter-level context leakage.

retrieval_preset.title: Retrieval Preset
retrieval_preset.description: Deep search defaults to the 'wide' retrieval-budget preset (see SearchConfig.retrieval_preset).

retrieval_budget.description: Explicit retrieval budget override, e.g. for evals/debug. Takes precedence over `retrieval_preset` when the `context_engine_luna_models` flag is on; ignored (like `retrieval_preset`) when it is off.

analysis_model.title: Analysis Model
analysis_model.description: OpenAI model used for combined relevance/sufficiency/refinement analysis.

synthesis_model.title: Synthesis Model
synthesis_model.description: Gemini model used to synthesize the grounded answer with numbered citations.

output_format.title: Output Format
output_format.description: Synthesis output format. ``md`` (default) returns a markdown answer with inline ``[N]`` citations; ``json`` returns a strict-schema ``StructuredAnswer`` populated under ``structured_answer`` with an empty ``answer`` string.

include_evidence.title: Include Evidence
include_evidence.description: When True (default), the response includes the numbered evidence blocks that ground the answer and synthesis is instructed to cite them. When False, evidence is still used internally for grounding but the response ``evidence`` field is ``[]``, the synthesis prompt does NOT instruct citation usage, and any leaked citation markers are stripped from the answer.

DeepSearchConfig.title: DeepSearchConfig
DeepSearchConfig.description:
SearchConfig tuned for exhaustive retrieval.

Same deterministic retrieve->analyze->synthesize pipeline as SearchConfig,
with both supported tools enabled by default and larger iteration/output
budgets (including a higher default minimum iteration count).

query.title: Query
query.description: Required user question for the pipeline.

task_id.title: Task Id
task_id.description: Optional task/conversation scope. When omitted, the engine short-circuits to matter-only markdown.

deep_search_config.description: Deep-search pipeline overrides; defaults applied when omitted.

DeepSearchModeConfig.title: DeepSearchModeConfig
DeepSearchModeConfig.description: Config for ``mode='deep_search'``: deterministic pipeline with deep-search budgets.

DeepenStep.title: DeepenStep
DeepenStep.description:
Target of one deepen action.

AUTHORITIES runs the deepen agent (assembled here); CASES and COVERAGE are
routed by DeepenStepWorkflow to their existing workflows.

document_id.title: Document Id
document_id.description: UUID of the document to delete.

document_ids.title: Document Ids
document_ids.description: Loose file UUIDs to delete. Use select_all for larger deletes.

folder_ids.title: Folder Ids
folder_ids.description: Folders to delete; each resolved recursively (whole subtree) on the server.

matter_id.title: Matter Id
matter_id.description: Scope for folder resolution: matter id for matter-scoped folders; omit for DocHub scope.

select_all.title: Select All
select_all.description: Delete all documents in the scope. With matter_id: all docs in the matter owned by the caller. Without matter_id: all visible user-owned docs (DocHub scope). When select_all_folder_id is also set, only docs under that folder subtree are deleted. document_ids and folder_ids are ignored.

select_all_folder_id.title: Select All Folder Id
select_all_folder_id.description: Scope select_all to a specific folder subtree. Only effective when select_all is true.

exclude_doc_ids.title: Exclude Doc Ids
exclude_doc_ids.description: Doc IDs to exclude from select_all. Used for the mode+delta selection model: the user selected all, then unchecked a few items. Bounded by user clicks (max 5000). Only effective when select_all is true.

exclude_folder_ids.title: Exclude Folder Ids
exclude_folder_ids.description: Folder IDs to exclude from select_all. The server resolves each folder's subtree and excludes all contained docs. Bounded by user clicks (max 500). Only effective when select_all is true.

prune_empty_folders.title: Prune Empty Folders
prune_empty_folders.description: If true, once the background purge finishes, delete the folders these documents vacated (and their ancestors) if they are left empty. Runs at the tail of the delete job, so it can't race the async purge, and never touches unrelated empty folders.

DeleteDocumentsRequest.title: DeleteDocumentsRequest
DeleteDocumentsRequest.description:
Request for POST delete-documents: hard-delete a batch of documents owned by the caller.

Accepts ``folder_ids`` (resolved server-side to all files in the subtree) and/or
``document_ids`` (loose files). At least one must be non-empty. When ``folder_ids``
is provided, ``matter_id`` scopes the resolution; omit it for DocHub scope.

Backward-compatible: the old ``document_ids``-only shape still works unchanged.

accepted.title: Accepted
accepted.description: Documents tombstoned and enrolled in the background purge.

workflow_id.title: Workflow Id
workflow_id.description: Id of the drain workflow (None if nothing accepted).

failed.title: Failed
failed.description: Documents rejected before tombstoning (not found or not the owner). Capped at 100 entries.

failed_count.title: Failed Count
failed_count.description: Total rejected documents, including any not listed in failed.

DeleteDocumentsResponse.title: DeleteDocumentsResponse
DeleteDocumentsResponse.description:
Result for POST delete-documents (async, ENG-17809).

The selected docs are tombstoned synchronously (they vanish from listings at
once) and purged in the background by a Temporal workflow. ``failed`` holds
only docs rejected before tombstoning (not found / not the owner / an archive
still being extracted).

unlinked_doc_count.title: Unlinked Doc Count
unlinked_doc_count.description: Matter scope: docs un-associated from the matter (still in DocHub).

hard_deleted_doc_count.title: Hard Deleted Doc Count
hard_deleted_doc_count.description: DocHub scope: docs hard-deleted (their only placement was inside the subtree).

pruned_folder_count.title: Pruned Folder Count
pruned_folder_count.description: When prune_empty_folders=true: folders pruned inline (matter scope, or DocHub with no async purge). None means pruning was deferred to the background drain (DocHub with files to purge) or wasn't requested.

transactions_updated.title: Transactions Updated
transactions_updated.description: Number of transactions that had flags removed

pending.title: Pending
pending.description: Documents still being purged (delete_state='deleting', or 'purging' once the drain claims them).

DeleteStatusResponse.title: DeleteStatusResponse
DeleteStatusResponse.description: Result for GET delete-status: counts sourced from delete_state (no Temporal query).

folder_ids.title: Folder Ids
folder_ids.description: Folders to delete; each resolved recursively (whole subtree).

matter_id.title: Matter Id
matter_id.description: Scope: matter id for matter-scoped folders/files; omit for DocHub scope.

DeletionImpactRequest.title: DeletionImpactRequest
DeletionImpactRequest.description: Request for POST deletion-impact: read-only preview of what a delete would affect.

matters.title: Matters
matters.description: Distinct matters any affected file is linked to; [] if none.

DeletionImpactResponse.title: DeletionImpactResponse
DeletionImpactResponse.description:
Result for POST deletion-impact: read-only; mutates nothing.

``total_file_count`` is every file under the folders (recursive) plus the loose
files, de-duped across multi-placements. ``matters`` is the union of distinct
matters any affected file is linked to (empty if none) — so the UI can warn that
deleting also removes those files from the listed matters.

causes_of_action.title: Causes Of Action
causes_of_action.description: The cause(s) of action underlying the demand.

legal_bases.title: Legal Bases
legal_bases.description: Legal bases from the existing Matter Analysis supporting the demand.

demand.title: Demand
demand.description: Explicit statement of the action or remedy sought.

deadline.title: Deadline
deadline.description: Compliance deadline (UTC), balancing urgency with feasibility.

demands.title: Demands
demands.description: A list of strategically crafted demands, underpinned by legal rationale.

DependentAllocationMember.description: Share percentages for one dependent (maps to dependents table).

capabilities.title: Capabilities

DetailDatasetResponse.description: Dataset response with additional details, such as document filenames for import benchmark

conversation_id.description: Graph conversation id of the open thread.

message_id.title: Message Id
message_id.description: Graph id of the message being replied to, when the pane has one. A reply being composed has no id of its own until it is saved.

thread_messages.title: Thread Messages
thread_messages.description: Messages the pane found in the open thread.

DetectMatterRequest.title: DetectMatterRequest
DetectMatterRequest.description: What the pane knows about the message being replied to.

source.title: Source
source.description: How the matter was established: 'folder' when a connected Outlook folder answered it, 'none' when nothing matched and the pane must ask the user to choose, 'ambiguous' when the folder is linked to several matters and the user must pick one of ``candidates``.

has_matters.title: Has Matters
has_matters.description: Whether the caller can view any matter at all. False lets the pane offer Create Matter instead of a picker with nothing in it. Only meaningful when no matter was detected; a detected matter implies True.

candidates.title: Candidates
candidates.description: When source is 'ambiguous': the matters the thread could belong to, in the order the picker should list them. Empty otherwise.

candidate_source.title: Candidate Source
candidate_source.description: Which lookup produced the match — ``candidates`` when ambiguous, ``matter`` otherwise: 'folder' when a connected Outlook folder answered, 'thread' when this thread was already synced into the matter(s). The pane words the pinned-group heading and the card's 'Detected from …' line from this, so neither can claim a folder connection that does not exist. Defaults to 'folder', which is what every caller assumed before this field existed.

DetectMatterResponse.title: DetectMatterResponse
DetectMatterResponse.description: The matter the open thread belongs to, if it can be established.

DocAgentDebugConversationMessageRow.title: DocAgentDebugConversationMessageRow
DocAgentDebugConversationMessageRow.description:
One persisted Smart Bot ``Message`` row, decoded through
``smart_bot.services.history.rebuild_agent_history`` — see
``GET /doc-agent-debug/runs/{run_id}/conversation``.

``content`` is the raw Anthropic-style history entry's ``content``
verbatim — a plain string, or a list of ``text``/``tool_use``/
``tool_result``/``ask_user`` blocks — passed through with no reshaping,
matching this package's "raw persisted shape, no second schema"
convention (see :class:`DocAgentDebugTraceResponse`).

DocAgentDebugConversationResponse.title: DocAgentDebugConversationResponse
DocAgentDebugConversationResponse.description:
``GET /doc-agent-debug/runs/{run_id}/conversation``: the run's
conversation, decoded up to the run's own ``UpdatedAt``, with the
``generate_word_document`` tool call that started this run pinned via
``is_draft_handoff`` when it could be identified (exactly, by the
resolved draft workflow id's ledger key; or, failing that, by being the
single such call in the window, or the closest in time to the run's
``CreatedAt``) — see ``conversation.get_run_conversation``.
``draft_handoff_message_index`` and ``draft_handoff_args`` are ``None``
when no ``generate_word_document`` call could be found in the window at
all (e.g. history predating the ``Index`` column, or a run started some
other way).

DocAgentDebugCostBreakdown.title: DocAgentDebugCostBreakdown
DocAgentDebugCostBreakdown.description: Exact-cost resolution result for one run — see ``run_links._resolve_cost``.

DocAgentDebugDraftHandoffArgs.title: DocAgentDebugDraftHandoffArgs
DocAgentDebugDraftHandoffArgs.description:
The ``generate_word_document`` tool-call args on the message pinned as
this run's handoff — see ``conversation._find_draft_handoff``. ``None``
fields mean that arg simply wasn't passed on the call (``template_doc_id``
is intentionally omitted here; it isn't part of what a debug reader needs
pinned alongside the handoff).

DocAgentDebugFailingToolRow.title: DocAgentDebugFailingToolRow
DocAgentDebugFailingToolRow.description:
One ``(tool, error message)`` bucket from the top-10 failing-tools table.

``tool`` is ``None`` for a supervisor-level ``error`` event (a model-call
failure with no specific tool attached) rather than a step-level tool
error — see ``get_top_failing_tools``.

DocAgentDebugModelPriceRow.title: DocAgentDebugModelPriceRow
DocAgentDebugModelPriceRow.description:
Per-million-token USD rates for one model — mirrors one entry of
``services/pricing.py``'s ``MODEL_PRICING``.

DocAgentDebugOutputDownloadRow.title: DocAgentDebugOutputDownloadRow
DocAgentDebugOutputDownloadRow.description:
A resolved output's signed download URL — one row per
``DocAgentDebugRunLinks.outputs`` entry, signed with the same
account/expiry/content-disposition approach as
``doc_agent_v2/routes/router.py``'s ``doc_agent_output`` route (see
``service._sign_output_download``). ``filename`` is the run-id-prefixed
name (``"{run_id}-{name}"``) baked into the signed URL's
``Content-Disposition`` header, so a browser download always lands with
that name regardless of what the URL's query string carries.

DocAgentDebugOutputRow.title: DocAgentDebugOutputRow
DocAgentDebugOutputRow.description:
One ``doc_metadata`` row matched to a run as one of its drafted outputs —
see ``run_links.resolve_run_links``.

``storage_account_alias``/``storage_container`` (plus ``location``) are the
exact three fields ``doc_storage.blob_ref_from_doc_metadata`` needs to build
a ``BlobRef`` for signing a download URL (see ``service._sign_output_download``);
kept alongside the display fields rather than requiring a second DocMetadata
fetch just to sign what this resolver already read once.

DocAgentDebugOverviewDayRow.title: DocAgentDebugOverviewDayRow
DocAgentDebugOverviewDayRow.description:
One day's aggregate row for ``GET /doc-agent-debug/overview`` — see
``routes/router.py`` and ``platform/queries/doc_agent_v2_run.py``'s
``get_overview_day_rows``.

``avg_*``/``p50_*``/``p95_*`` fields are ``None`` for a day with no
matching rows (Postgres ``AVG``/``percentile_cont`` over an empty set),
not ``0`` — a debug chart should render a gap, not a false zero.

DocAgentDebugOverviewResponse.title: DocAgentDebugOverviewResponse
DocAgentDebugOverviewResponse.description:
The 21-day aggregate — default shape of ``GET /doc-agent-debug/overview``
when no ``status``/``date`` drill-down filter is given.

DocAgentDebugOverviewRunRow.title: DocAgentDebugOverviewRunRow
DocAgentDebugOverviewRunRow.description:
One run in a drill-down list (``?status=``/``?date=``) — deliberately
thinner than :class:`DocAgentDebugRunView`, which is for inspecting a
single run, not listing many.

DocAgentDebugOverviewRunsResponse.title: DocAgentDebugOverviewRunsResponse
DocAgentDebugOverviewRunsResponse.description:
Drill-down shape of ``GET /doc-agent-debug/overview`` when ``status``
and/or ``date`` is given: the matching run list instead of the aggregate.

DocAgentDebugPricingResponse.title: DocAgentDebugPricingResponse
DocAgentDebugPricingResponse.description:
Snapshot of ``services/pricing.py``'s pricing table for the debug
UI's client-side token-count -> estimated-cost math on the live
(unpersisted) test-run path, which has no ``model_usage_ledger`` row to
read a real cost from (see ``GET /doc-agent-debug/pricing``).

DocAgentDebugResolvedInputs.title: DocAgentDebugResolvedInputs
DocAgentDebugResolvedInputs.description:
The draft's original inputs, resolved from Temporal history or, failing
that, guessed from the first persisted user trace message — see
``run_links._resolve_inputs``. Any field may be ``None`` even when this
object itself is present: the trace-fallback text only contains the
title/instructions/user-request, never ``template_doc_id`` or
``authored_content`` (those are just noted as present in the prompt, not
echoed verbatim).

chat_turn_workflow_ids_unresolved_reason.title: Chat Turn Workflow Ids Unresolved Reason

DocAgentDebugRunLinks.title: DocAgentDebugRunLinks
DocAgentDebugRunLinks.description:
Everything ``resolve_run_links`` could derive for one run, each
sub-resolution independently best-effort (see ``run_links.py``'s module
docstring): a failed lookup leaves its field empty/``None`` and sets the
matching ``*_unresolved_reason`` instead of failing the whole response.

DocAgentDebugRunRequest.title: DocAgentDebugRunRequest
DocAgentDebugRunRequest.description:
Mirrors the smart-bot ``draft_document`` tool payload (see
``temporal/activities/doc_agent_v2/draft.py``'s ``DraftDocumentInput``),
plus a client-tunable (but server-clamped) iteration cap.

DocAgentDebugRunView.title: DocAgentDebugRunView
DocAgentDebugRunView.description:
Read-only view of a persisted ``DocAgentV2Run`` (M3a) for
``GET /doc-agent-debug/runs/{run_id}`` and
``GET /doc-agent-debug/runs`` — see ``routes/router.py``.

``state``/``versions``/``tracking`` are ``DocAgentV2Run``'s ``State``/
``Versions``/``Tracking`` JSONB columns verbatim (no reshaping): this
is an inspection tool, not a second schema to keep in sync with
``services/run.py``'s payload shapes. ``state["semantic_doc"]`` is the
full ``SemanticDoc`` dump for this run's document — the debug tool's
"download semantic doc" affordance reads it straight from here rather
than a second field, since it is already the full JSON, not a summary.

``links``/``output_downloads`` are new (M3a "downloads"/"search-share"):
``links`` is ``run_links.resolve_run_links``'s full best-effort output —
outputs, workflow ids, resolved inputs, exact cost — and
``output_downloads`` is one signed SAS URL per ``links.outputs`` entry,
both run-id-prefixed. Unlike the overview route, this view inspects one
run at a time, so calling the resolver (and, per-output, signing a URL)
here is the intended cost — see ``run_links.py``'s module docstring on
why the *overview* route avoids it instead.

DocAgentDebugSearchResponse.title: DocAgentDebugSearchResponse
DocAgentDebugSearchResponse.description:
``GET /doc-agent-debug/runs/search``: up to 50 runs, newest first.

``truncated`` is ``True`` when more than 50 rows matched — the search
box's own hint to narrow with ``status``/``from``/``to`` rather than a
silent, misleadingly-complete-looking list of exactly 50.

DocAgentDebugSearchRunRow.title: DocAgentDebugSearchRunRow
DocAgentDebugSearchRunRow.description:
One matched run for ``GET /doc-agent-debug/runs/search`` — see
``search.search_runs``. Deliberately thin, like
:class:`DocAgentDebugOverviewRunRow`; the full run detail (outputs,
inputs, cost, conversation, Temporal) is one click away via ``id``.

``matched_document_name`` is set only when this run matched the search
box's ``q`` through a document-name source (a ``doc_metadata`` output
name, a ``DocAgentSession.OutputFilename``, or a trace-parsed draft
title) — ``None`` when the run matched some other way (exact run/
conversation/user id, or exact email) or when no ``q`` was given at all.

DocAgentDebugTraceResponse.title: DocAgentDebugTraceResponse
DocAgentDebugTraceResponse.description:
Read-only page of a persisted run's trace records — see
``GET /doc-agent-debug/runs/{run_id}/trace``.

``records`` are the raw persisted ``DocAgentV2RunTrace.payload`` dicts
verbatim (the same ``event``/``step``/``message``/``semantic``/``final``
wire shape the live debug SSE stream emits — see ``service.py``'s module
docstring and ``app/modules/doc_agent_v2/services/trace/records.py``'s
``TraceRecordProducer``): no reshaping, so there is no second schema to
keep in sync. This is also the exact shape ``GET .../bundle`` embeds as
its ``{run_id}-trace.json`` entry — see ``service.build_run_bundle``.

``next_seq`` is the ``Seq`` of the last row in this page (or ``None``
when ``records`` is empty), for cursor-based paging — pass it straight
back as the next call's ``after_seq``. An empty ``records`` list with
``next_seq=None`` means the run has no more records past the requested
cursor.

DocAgentDebugUsageLedgerRow.title: DocAgentDebugUsageLedgerRow
DocAgentDebugUsageLedgerRow.description: One ``model_usage_ledger`` row, for the run inspection routes below.

DocAgentDebugWorkflowIdRow.title: DocAgentDebugWorkflowIdRow
DocAgentDebugWorkflowIdRow.description:
One Temporal workflow id linked to a run.

``matched_by_time`` is always ``True`` for chat-turn ids today (Smart Bot's
chat-turn billing prefix is the run id, not a workflow id, so there is no
exact key to match on — see ``run_links.py``'s module docstring); kept as
a field rather than a hardcoded constant so a future exact-match source
(e.g. a workflow id persisted somewhere) can set it ``False`` without a
schema change.

DocAgentDebugWorkflowStatusRow.title: DocAgentDebugWorkflowStatusRow
DocAgentDebugWorkflowStatusRow.description:
One resolved workflow id's live Temporal status — see
``GET /doc-agent-debug/runs/{run_id}/workflows``.

``status`` mirrors ``temporal/utils/workflow_status.py``'s
``query_basic_workflow_status`` mapping (``"processing"``/``"completed"``/
``"failed"``), plus ``"unknown"`` when the lookup itself failed here (see
``unresolved_reason``, set instead of raising — matching this package's
per-field best-effort convention). ``workflow_type`` is this module's own
label (``"draft"``/``"chat_turn"``, matching
:class:`DocAgentDebugWorkflowIdRow`); ``temporal_workflow_type`` is the
actual registered Temporal workflow type name read off a plain
``describe()`` call.

DocAgentDebugWorkflowsResponse.title: DocAgentDebugWorkflowsResponse
DocAgentDebugWorkflowsResponse.description:
``GET /doc-agent-debug/runs/{run_id}/workflows``: live Temporal status
for every workflow id ``run_links.resolve_run_links`` resolved for this
run, plus plain-English diagnostics where Temporal and the run's own
``Status`` disagree (a workflow closed while the run is still
``"running"``, or the run is ``"done"`` while a resolved workflow's
terminal status was a failure — the latter happens because the draft
activity writes ``"done"`` before it uploads the output file; see
``temporal/activities/doc_agent_v2/draft.py``) — see
``service._workflow_mismatches``.

estimated_credits.title: Estimated Credits

estimated_seconds.title: Estimated Seconds

DocumentEstimateItem.title: DocumentEstimateItem
DocumentEstimateItem.description: Per-document credit estimate returned by the estimation endpoint.

DocumentEstimateRequest.title: DocumentEstimateRequest
DocumentEstimateRequest.description: Request for POST /document/estimate: estimate processing credits before upload.

total_credits.title: Total Credits
total_credits.description: Total estimated credits for all files, rounded up once for the batch.

total_tokens.title: Total Tokens
total_tokens.description: Total estimated tokens across all files.

estimate_min_seconds.title: Estimate Min Seconds
estimate_min_seconds.description: Lower bound of estimated total processing time in seconds.

estimate_max_seconds.title: Estimate Max Seconds
estimate_max_seconds.description: Upper bound of estimated total processing time in seconds.

empirical.title: Empirical

credits_pending.title: Credits Pending
credits_pending.description: Credits already reserved by the caller's in-flight uploads this month.

credits_remaining.title: Credits Remaining
credits_remaining.description: Credits left in the caller's monthly budget.

would_exceed_budget.title: Would Exceed Budget
would_exceed_budget.description: True when total_credits + credits_pending exceeds credits_remaining. Computed the same way the registration gate computes it, so a False here means the upload will be accepted. Clients must block the upload when this is True.

DocumentEstimateResponse.title: DocumentEstimateResponse
DocumentEstimateResponse.description: Response for POST /document/estimate: per-document and aggregate credit estimates.

DocumentFilterOptionsResponse.title: DocumentFilterOptionsResponse

seed_causes_of_action.title: Seed Causes Of Action

Render this rather than parsing the name — the folder listing's type sort uses the same derivation, and parsing the name yourself puts the label out of step with the ordering. parent_id.description: Document this one was extracted from: an archive member's archive, or an email attachment's email. Null for a file added on its own.

Populated by the single-document metadata endpoint only — listings omit it to keep the page payload down. Null when the document is not an email attachment, or when its email predates provenance being recorded. Equal to `email_sources[0].provenance` when `email_sources` is non-empty; kept as its own field for clients that only need the one message.

email_sources.title: Email Sources
email_sources.description: Every email this document arrived on that the caller may see, not just the first (ENG-22887). A deduplicated attachment is stored once but can have been delivered by several messages. Ordered: the document's own parent email first — so the head is the message the 'Extracted from' label names — then oldest *ingested* first, which is send order only for a mailbox synced in order; sort on `provenance.sent_at` if you need true chronology. More than one entry means the file was received more than once. Empty for a document that is not an email attachment, and on listing endpoints, which omit it.

email_sources_truncated.title: Email Sources Truncated
email_sources_truncated.description: True when more emails carried this document than `email_sources` lists (the cap is 25). The count of the remainder is deliberately not reported — it would cost a second query for a number the panel does not need. Always false on listing endpoints.

processed_tokens.title: Processed Tokens
processed_tokens.description: Tokens ingestion actually produced for this document (the OCR/parse output), from the usage ledger. Null until processing has recorded usage. Lets a client compare its own pre-upload count with what was billed.

credits_charged.title: Credits Charged
credits_charged.description: Credits charged for this document across ingestion and summarization, from the usage ledger. Null until recorded.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: ID of the user who uploaded the document.

can_edit.title: Can Edit

ingestion_status.description: Derived per-doc ingestion status. Projected from DocMetadata.status and the latest INGEST DocHubJob. Values: queued, processing, done, failed, stranded, unknown.

failure_reason.title: Failure Reason
failure_reason.description: Populated when ingestion_status is 'failed'; short machine-readable reason (e.g. 'password_protected').

archive_members_total.title: Archive Members Total
archive_members_total.description: Archives only: how many files the archive holds, known once extraction has planned its members. Null for ordinary documents and for archives that have not started extracting. NOT cleared when extraction finishes, so a fully processed archive keeps its final total; read it only alongside ingestion_status.

archive_members_done.title: Archive Members Done
archive_members_done.description: Archives only: how many members have been registered as documents so far. Climbs while ingestion_status is 'processing'; on 'failed' it is how many files did land. NOT cleared when extraction finishes, so a processed archive keeps its final n of N — do not read it as 'still extracting' without checking ingestion_status.

already_linked_to_task.title: Already Linked To Task
already_linked_to_task.description: True if this document is already linked to the specified task_id. Only populated when linked_task_id is provided in the request; null otherwise.

DocumentMetadataSummary.description: Abbreviated document metadata for API responses (subset of DocMetadata).

failure_reason.title: Failure Reason
failure_reason.description: Why the document failed (e.g. 'password_protected'). Only set on FAILED_NO_RETRY.

retry_pending.title: Retry Pending

DocumentPollItem.description: Single document polling result: id, status, size, and percent_complete.

DocumentReference.description: A user-selected document with optional contextualization.

DocumentResponse.description: The document modal response based on our SQLAlchemy model.

DraftContextSelection.description: Which sources the user left checked in the pane.

DraftDocumentInputs.title: DraftDocumentInputs
DraftDocumentInputs.description:
What the attorney supplied at intake for the chosen draft type.

Keyed by the role each plays in generation. Mirrors the per-type generate-request
fields so the drafting step / draft-direct job consumes them directly. See ENG-15499.

Every field is optional and per-type: the Hub config panel for the chosen type decides
which ones intake renders, and a type with no use for one leaves it None. Persisted as
JSONB (legal_research_v3.draft_document_inputs), so new members are additive — no migration.

DraftDocumentType.title: DraftDocumentType
DraftDocumentType.description:
The document an attorney intends to draft, captured at intake.

Values match the work-products generation keys so the drafting step / draft-direct
job can map a chosen type to its generator and input slots. See ENG-15499.

One member per Draft Hub type that has a real generation endpoint, so intake can offer
everything the Hub can produce. The FE mirror is DOC_TYPE_REGISTRY's ``intakeValue``
(docTypeRegistry.ts) — adding a member here without one there leaves it unselectable.
Deliberately absent: the Hub's three dialog wizards (custom Email / custom Demand Letter /
custom Motion) each generate over client-driven SSE with no server-side job, so there is
nothing a post-run trigger could start and leave running to completion.

DraftEnrichmentEntry.title: DraftEnrichmentEntry
DraftEnrichmentEntry.description: Per-draft entry in the batch enrichment-status polling response.

instruction.description: The user's own wording. Required when mode is custom.

DraftRefine.title: DraftRefine
DraftRefine.description:
A follow-up instruction applied to a draft the user already has.

``previous_draft`` is sent by the pane rather than held server-side: the pane
owns the draft the user is looking at, including one they refined and then
restored with Original, so it is the only reliable source of what to change.

conversation_id.description: Graph conversation id of the open thread. When present the server fetches the thread from Graph, which yields real sender, recipient, date and body fields; ``thread`` below is then only a fallback.

thread.description: The thread as the pane read it out of the compose window. Used only when Graph cannot supply it — the quoted block's shape differs per Outlook client, so it is the less reliable of the two sources.

DraftThread.title: DraftThread
DraftThread.description: The email thread the reply belongs to. The first message is the one being replied to.

EmailDraftResponse.description:

All-None rather than a 404: "nothing saved yet" is the ordinary first-open state of the wizard,
not an error, and the client opens the dialog the same way either way.

EmailDraftSaveRequest.title: EmailDraftSaveRequest
EmailDraftSaveRequest.description: The wizard's current state: the email it is showing, and the form that produced it.

sent_at.description: The Date header, as an ISO 8601 string. A string rather than a timestamp because a sender whose client wrote a malformed date is passed through verbatim rather than dropped — parse it if you can, otherwise render it as text.

message_id.title: Message Id
message_id.description: RFC 5322 Message-ID, angle brackets included. The same value in every mailbox holding a copy.

EmailProvenance.title: EmailProvenance
EmailProvenance.description:
The message an attachment arrived on (ENG-22885).

Recorded on the email document when its attachments were extracted, and read
here through ``parent_id``. Every field is optional because it mirrors the
headers the message actually carried: an email with no ``Cc`` has none, and a
message whose headers could not be decoded has nothing at all.

Absent entirely for a file that is not an email attachment, and for one whose
email was ingested before the extractor recorded provenance — re-ingesting
that email fills it in.

provenance.description: That email's own headers. Fields the message did not carry are null/empty.

EmailSource.title: EmailSource
EmailSource.description:
One email a document arrived on, as the details panel lists it (ENG-22887).

A deduplicated attachment is stored once but can have arrived on several
emails; each of them recorded the document id it resolved to, and that is the
only record the file came more than once. Listing them is what lets a matter
trace the file back to every message that delivered it, rather than to
whichever one happened to be resolved first.

``document_id`` is the email's own Doc Hub document, so a client can open it.

created_at.description: Folder creation time — the folder-side analogue of a file's upload_datetime, and what sort_by=date_added orders folders by. Render this in a 'Date Added' column so the sort is visible.

FolderSortField.title: FolderSortField
FolderSortField.description:
Sortable fields for the folder listing (ENG-19278).

Deliberately not the same set as ``DocumentSortField``: ``size`` isn't a column in the
folder browser, while ``added_by`` and ``type`` are. Matters/Tasks are absent on purpose —
those names are encrypted at rest, so ordering on them would sort ciphertext.

Folders are sorted together with files, never pinned above them. How a folder places depends
on whether it has a value for the field:

- ``NAME``, ``DATE_ADDED`` — a folder has its own name and ``created_at``, so it interleaves
  with files on equal footing.
- ``TYPE`` — a folder sorts as the literal ``"folder"``, so it interleaves alphabetically
  among file extensions (``docx`` < ``folder`` < ``pdf``).
- ``CATEGORY``, ``ADDED_BY`` — a folder has neither, so it carries NULL and pins to the top
  in *both* directions (see ``_merged_order_by``).

FolderTreeResponse.title: FolderTreeResponse
FolderTreeResponse.description:
Lightweight folder-only tree for the folder-picker dialog (ENG-22636).

Returns every folder in the scope as a flat list; the client rebuilds the
tree from parent_id pointers. No files, no counts, no pagination — just
the skeleton needed to render a destination picker.

write sites so a typo can't silently open a new bucket. Values are exact, byte-for-byte
matches of the strings already persisted; do NOT rename/renumber members, that would orphan
existing rows. Distinct from ``DraftDocumentType`` above (an intake *intent*, e.g. its
DEMAND_LETTER spells "demand-letter-document") and from the unrelated ``DocumentType`` in
``intake.document_analysis.types`` (input-document classification).

RealPropertyUpdateRequest.title: RealPropertyUpdateRequest
RealPropertyUpdateRequest.description:
Body for ``PATCH /forensic/{dataset_id}/real-estate/residences/{property_id}``.

All fields optional — only those the attorney explicitly sets are written;
``None`` means "don't change" (the schema can't clear a populated field).
Mirrors the vehicle update endpoint:

- ``estimated_value`` is the primary use case — the pipeline creates a
  residence from a deed / 1098 with no current value. On any change it's
  stamped ``estimated_value_source="owner_estimate"`` server-side and
  appended to ``metadata_ex.valuations`` history, and propagated to the
  property's balance-sheet item unless that row is locked.
- Identity / classification / acquisition fields cover extractor
  corrections. Editing any address component re-syncs
  ``normalized_address_key`` so cross-document dedup stays consistent.

This endpoint does NOT lock the property — to pin a value against later
auto-extracted appraisals, lock the balance-sheet row (BSI ``is_locked``).

SearchScope.title: SearchScope
SearchScope.description:
How deep a folder-listing query reaches (ENG-23085).

Query mode (any ``search`` or file filter) flattens the listing into a match set. This
chooses what that set spans:

- ``SUBTREE`` — matches at and below ``folder_id`` (the whole scope at root). The default,
  and the only behaviour before this flag existed, so an absent param is a no-op.
- ``CURRENT`` — matches placed directly at ``folder_id``: its immediate child folders and
  the files at that level, nothing deeper.

The endpoint holds no policy about which affordance maps to which value — the frontend
sends ``CURRENT`` for filter chips and ``SUBTREE`` for search (ENG-23088). Keeping the
mapping there means a scope control, if one is ever wanted, overrides this param without
a backend change.

The restriction is applied in the query, never after paging: a page filtered post-hoc
would render short or empty and make ``has_next`` describe rows the caller never sees.

ownership_type.description:
Single-field summary of who owns this vehicle.

``individual`` = at least one personal owner; ``entity`` = held by a
business (trust / LLC / S-Corp); ``both`` = mixed; ``unknown``
= no owners attached yet.

primary_owner_name.description:
Single-name fallback when the UI can't render the full owners list.

Prefers ``title_holder`` > ``co_title_holder`` > ``trust`` >
``corporate``, then highest ownership_percentage, then first owner
by id. Returns None when no owners exist.

display_label.title: Display Label
display_label.description:
Human-readable label for table rows and matter-memory bullets.

Fallback chain: ``year make model`` → ``make model`` → ``VIN xxx`` →
``Vehicle``. Mirrors ``_build_bsi_name`` in the persistence layer so
the API label matches the BSI ``name`` column.

title_status_label.title: Title Status Label
title_status_label.description:
Map ``has_lienholder`` + ``title_brands`` to the ``VehicleTitleStatus``
contract — same logic as the persistence helper so the UI can show the
title status without re-deriving it client-side.

``"clean"`` requires *positive title evidence* — at least one of
``title_number`` / ``title_issuing_state`` / ``title_issue_date`` /
``title_brands`` populated. Vehicles created from a KBB / BeenVerified
valuation alone (no title uploaded yet) have all four nulled out and
report ``"unknown"`` — absence of warning signals isn't proof of a
clean title.

VehicleOwnerResponse.title: VehicleOwnerResponse
VehicleOwnerResponse.description:

joint title (``Jane AND John Doe``), trustee + beneficiary, lessor + lessee.

``taxpayer_id`` is null until the post-extraction linking pass matches the
owner name against a canonical taxpayer in the dataset (deterministic
matcher — see ``link_vehicle_owners_to_taxpayers_activity``). Stays null
when no confident match exists (ambiguity / no matching taxpayer yet).
``owner_name`` is always populated.

VehicleResponse.title: VehicleResponse
VehicleResponse.description:
A titled motor vehicle — car / truck / motorcycle / trailer / RV.

Same identity / lifecycle shape as ``RealPropertyResponse`` so the UI can
render both in unified asset lists.

``has_lienholder=False`` is the conclusive paid-off signal — the only
document that can prove a vehicle is owned free and clear. ``title_brands``
captures Salvage / Rebuilt / Flood / Lemon / etc. (empty list = clean title).

VehicleUpdateRequest.title: VehicleUpdateRequest
VehicleUpdateRequest.description:
Body for ``PATCH /forensic/{dataset_id}/vehicles/{vehicle_id}``.

All fields optional — only those the attorney explicitly sets are
written. ``None`` means "don't change"; the request schema cannot be
used to clear a populated field (a future ``clear_fields`` parameter
can add that when there's a use case).

Per the design call on ENG-12939: this endpoint does **not** lock the
Vehicle row. A subsequent auto-extracted KBB / title with a newer
``as_of_date`` will run through the standard merge policy and may
overwrite the attorney's entry. If the attorney wants a value to stick,
they lock the row on the balance sheet (BSI ``is_locked=True``), which
prevents this endpoint's BSI propagation from touching ``current_amount``.

Manual ``estimated_value`` entries are recorded as
``valuation_source="owner_estimate"`` in the historical valuations list
so the UI can render attorney-entered values alongside auto-extracted
KBB / NADA / BeenVerified entries.

WizardDraftKind.title: WizardDraftKind
WizardDraftKind.description:
Which streaming wizard a saved row belongs to.

Values are the ``{kind}`` path segment. Distinct from ``GeneratedDocumentType``: these name a
*wizard's working state*, not a filed document — a MOTION row here coexists with that motion's
own ``generated_documents`` row rather than replacing it.

WizardDraftResponse.title: WizardDraftResponse
WizardDraftResponse.description:
The saved draft, or all-None when this wizard has never saved one for this research.

All-None rather than a 404: "nothing saved yet" is the ordinary first-open state of a wizard,
not an error, and the client opens the dialog the same way either way.
